help.title: Help
help.what1: For indie developers and one-person companies: one human plus one agent, managing N machines.
help.what2: The default page is To-do, not a dashboard — it hands you the few things that need doing today, and stays quiet when nothing does.
help.onboardSubtitle: Three steps: server → enroll a machine → open the console
help.onboard1Note: First boot creates the CA, the SQLite database and a one-time bootstrap token (printed in the log). A persistent volume is required — without one every redeploy makes a new CA and every enrolled node drops off.
help.onboard2Note: From then on the node reports every 30 seconds, and its identity is its own Ed25519 key — every request is signed, so the transport layer carries no identity.
help.onboard3Cmd: cat <data-dir>/admin.token   # paste this token into the sign-in box
help.onboardPaas: Behind a platform that terminates TLS at the edge (Render, Railway), run the monitor with --plain-http (or ZHIWEI_PLAIN_HTTP=1). Nodes then verify against system roots instead of pinning a local CA.
help.aiSubtitle: Agents are first-class users of this system
help.ai1: The API base and credential live in Settings → AI access, along with a "Copy the brief for AI" button — paste it into your agent and it knows how to read this console.
help.ai2: Today that means calling the HTTP API directly, which any agent that can make HTTP requests can do: read endpoints take the Bearer admin token; actions go through POST /v1/exec, where the ops key signs the command, the node verifies it before running it, and signs the result back.
help.ai3: So your agent sees exactly what you see — it reads /v1/todo rather than a screenshot — and can trigger exactly the actions you can click, with no extra channel.
help.aiBoundary: Boundary: agents don't decide on their own. For destructive actions (shutdown, reboot, container removal, killing processes) have the agent state its intent and wait for your confirmation.
help.deploy1: Two shapes. Self-hosted (the default): the monitor terminates TLS itself. First boot generates a local CA and uses it to sign the monitor's own server certificate; enrolled nodes pin that CA and verify every later request against it.
help.deploy2: Behind a platform (Render, Railway): TLS is terminated at the edge, so run the monitor with --plain-http. The local CA then does nothing — the monitor's certificate is edge-issued, nodes verify against system roots, and enroll doesn't hand out a CA at all. The "Monitor's TLS certificate" section in Settings says so explicitly.
help.deploy3: Worth being clear about: in both shapes **node identity does not come from a certificate**. Every request is signed with the node's own Ed25519 key, and the monitor checks the signature plus a time window and replay protection; commands go the other way, signed by the ops key and verified by the node. TLS is transport encryption here, and changing deployment shape never weakens authentication.

settings.aiBrief:
# ZhiWei console API

Base: {{base}}
Auth: every request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`

## Read (GET)

- /v1/todo — the few things that need doing, bucketed as now / watch / recovered, each with a hint_key (what to do next)
- /v1/nodes — node list with the latest metric frame and online state
- /v1/nodes/<id>/series?metric=host.cpu.usage&from=<ms>&to=<ms>&limit=600 — trends; resolution=raw means 10-second data, hourly means hourly aggregates
- /v1/nodes/<id>/containers, /v1/containers — containers (compose project tags act as the "app" label)
- /v1/certificates — certificates and expiry
- /v1/services — services and probe state
- /v1/retention — retention policy (raw days, hourly days)

## Act (POST /v1/exec)

Body: {"node_id":"<id>","action":"<name>","params":{...}}
Actions: container_start / container_stop / container_restart / container_remove,
kill_process (params: pid, signal=term|kill), fetch_logs, restart_host, shutdown_host,
refresh_inventory, scan_certs
Result: GET /v1/commands/history, look up by command_id — state=done|failed, result_ok, result_text / result_error

## Boundaries

- Every action runs as a signed command: the ops key signs it, the node verifies before executing, and the node signs the result back.
- Do not run destructive actions (shutdown, reboot, container removal, killing processes) on your own — say what you intend to do and wait for confirmation.
- A container can only be removed once stopped; stop it first.
- Reboot and shutdown are delayed by one minute, leaving a window to cancel.
settings.pwSubtitle: Changing this key is the console's password change
settings.pwNote: This is the only key the console has (nodes use signatures and don't recognise it). It takes effect immediately, and this browser switches over too — no re-login.
settings.chTokenPlaceholder: leave empty for no auth header
settings.chTokenNote: If set, deliveries carry Authorization: Bearer <token> — useful for your own receiver. Feishu / DingTalk / Slack bot URLs are credentials themselves, so leave it empty.
settings.chTestOk: Test notification sent — check the receiving end
settings.caEdgeNote: TLS is terminated by an edge in this deployment, so this CA isn't used: the monitor's certificate is edge-issued and nodes no longer pin it (they use system roots). The fingerprint here is only a diagnostic.
